title: FORMAT statements use label numbers — moving them changes output layout if labels collide
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE PRINT_HEADER(A, B)
C     The WRITE references FORMAT 100. FORMAT 100 specifies
C     (1X, A8, F8.2) -- one blank, 8-char string, 8-char real
C     with 2 decimals. Removing or renumbering 100 silently changes
C     the output. Many legacy programs share FORMAT labels across
C     subroutines via INCLUDE, so the format used here may live in
C     a copybook.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      CHARACTER*8 A
      REAL        B
      WRITE (6, 100) A, B
  100 FORMAT (1X, A8, F8.2)
      END
notes: FORMAT label resolution + edit descriptors (Aw, Fw.d, Iw, Ew.d) are everywhere in legacy report-printing code. A Java rewrite using String.format must mirror the exact widths to keep downstream report parsers happy. Surface the descriptor list as the rewrite contract.
